title: BlockTree
description: The block-editor layout tree stored under a document template's `block_tree`. Discriminated unions are tagged by `type` (blocks, inline content) or `kind` (image source). Objects are intentionally open (additionalProperties not restricted) so forward-compatible keys are tolerated.
$comment: ASSEMBLY RULES for a generator. This tree is a page layout that a renderer turns byte-identically into PDF (Typst) and DOCX. (1) Top level: `blocks` is the document body, a flat ordered array; optional `settings` sets page size / margins / default font / spacing; optional `header`/`footer` carry running margin content repeated on every page. Field/key order on the wire is version, settings, header, footer, blocks (the frontend autosave dirty-check is a JSON.stringify compare, so emit keys in that order). (2) Every block object is `{ "id": <uuid v4>, "type": <discriminator>, ...kind-specific fields }` — `type` selects the branch of BlockKind. Inline content nodes inside `text`/`heading`/`blockquote` blocks are their OWN discriminated union, tagged by `type` too (text | link | plain | bold | italic | linebreak | tab | signature | field_ref | page_number | row_index). Image sources are tagged by `kind`. (3) Two table families: use data-bound `table` (array_path + columns) when rows come from a runtime array and you want one row per array item; use author-drawn `static_table` (explicit rows/cells with rich block content, merges, per-cell borders) when you hand-lay a fixed grid. A static_table row can itself loop via `loop_source`/`loop_as` (at most one per table), optionally naming a 1-based row counter via `loop_index_as`; an inline `row_index` token prints that counter and is refused anywhere outside a repeating row. (4) Dynamic values: an inline `field_ref` renders a bound value as literal plain text via a dotted `path` (e.g. "customer.name", "nodes.n1.output.total") OR an `expression` (a value-producing formula, same engine as computed fields / decision conditions; when present it wins and `path` is ignored — leave `path` as ""), with an optional `format` display mask. A `rich_text` BLOCK instead parses its bound value as Markdown and emits block structure (headings, lists, bold, links). A block-level `condition` is a truthy expression gating whether the block renders (if/else = two sibling blocks with complementary conditions). (5) `signature` inline nodes are markable void signing fields (drawn signature / initials / typed date-text-number / checkbox), reserving space in the flow. (6) Lengths are free-form strings with an explicit unit: absolute `mm|cm|pt|in` (e.g. "20mm", "12pt", "0.5cm", "8cm"), `leading` and `rule_gap` also allow `em` ("1em"), a run's `rule_width` also allows `%`, a signature `reserved_width` also allows a space count ("10sp"); only a per-block `margins` side may be negative; `line_height` is a unitless multiplier string ("1.5"); font sizes are a fixed allowlist of `Npt` strings. Colours are hex strings ("#1a2b3c"). PageBreak and inline Signature are rejected inside header/footer regions. (7) Sections: `settings.orientation` / `settings.margins` set up the FIRST run of pages; a TOP-LEVEL body `page_break` carrying `orientation` and/or `page_margins` opens a new section with that setup. Values are sticky (absent = inherit the preceding section), so a single landscape table is a pair of breaks — one `landscape` before it, one `portrait` after. A section-opening break may not carry a `condition` and may not sit inside a column or table cell. (8) Save also runs the assembler, which refuses: a heading `level` outside 1–3, a column_group with fewer than 2 or more than 4 columns, a data `table` with no columns, and a static_table with no rows or no columns.

version.description: Structural schema version, reserved for INCOMPATIBLE changes to the tree shape. New block kinds and new optional fields (settings, header, footer) are additive and do NOT bump this — leave it at the value the template was created with (commonly 1).

settings.description: Optional document-level page setup (page size, margins, default font + size, line/paragraph spacing, body justification). Absent → renderer defaults, byte-for-byte the pre-settings behaviour. Additive; presence does not bump `version`.

header.description: Optional Word-style running header repeated in the top margin of every page. Reuses the full Block model. Absent → no header. `page_number` inline tokens are meaningful here.

footer.description: Optional Word-style running footer repeated in the bottom margin of every page. Reuses the full Block model. Absent → no footer. Typical place for a "Trang X / Y" page-number line.

blocks.description: The document body: a flat, ordered list of blocks rendered top to bottom. Lists are expressed as consecutive blocks carrying the same `list_style` (there is no list container).

PageSetup.description: Document-level page setup. Every sub-field is optional and only present keys take effect; absent keys fall back to the renderer default. Length fields are non-negative and absolute (`mm|cm|pt|in`) except `leading` and `rule_gap`, which also permit `em`; a bad length is refused at save (`invalid_length`).

page_size.description: Paper size. Only "a4" is supported today. Absent → engine default.

orientation.description: Orientation of the document's FIRST section. Absent → portrait (what every template meant before orientation existed). A top-level `page_break` carrying its own `orientation` opens a later section the other way round.

margins.description: Page margins of the document's FIRST section, as non-negative absolute lengths (no `em`). Absent → engine default margins. A section-opening `page_break` may replace them via its `page_margins`.

default_font_family.description: Document default font family (from the body font allowlist). Individual runs may override it.

default_font_size.description: Document default font size (from the body size allowlist). Individual runs may override it.

leading.description: Line spacing WITHIN a paragraph (Typst par.leading). Also permits `em` (its DOCX mapping is approximate anyway). Absent → engine default.

space_before.description: Absolute space BEFORE each paragraph (DOCX w:before). Together with `space_after` forms the inter-paragraph gap.

space_after.description: Absolute space AFTER each paragraph (DOCX w:after; feeds Typst par.spacing). Legacy alias `paragraph_spacing` is also accepted on read and re-serialised under this canonical key.

justify.description: Document-wide body justification. true → justified body text; absent/false → left-aligned per the align defaults.

rule_gap.description: Gap between text and the line drawn by the `underline_rule` inline mark (NĐ30 gạch chân — a line below, not a touching underline). A non-negative length in `mm|cm|pt|in` or `em`. Absent → the renderer default.

rule_thickness.description: Document-wide `underline_rule` weight. Absolute length; absent → the renderer default (1pt), which the PDF and DOCX renderers are both pinned to so the two formats draw the same line. Word's line-weight ladder (0.25/0.5/0.75/1/1.5/2.25/3/4.5/6pt) is exactly the values that are whole eighths of a point — how OOXML stores a weight.

Margins.description: A four-sided inset (page margins, a section's `page_margins`, or a per-block inset). All four sides are required and are absolute length strings matching `-?<decimal>(mm|cm|pt|in)` (no `em`). The leading `-` is accepted only in a per-block `margins`; page margins and a section's `page_margins` must be non-negative.

HeaderFooter.description: Running header or footer content — a thin wrapper over the same Block list the body uses, so every block kind works in the margin region. A hard `page_break` and inline `signature` fields are rejected here at validation time (also when nested in a column or table cell).

blocks.description: Ordered blocks rendered in the running margin region on every page. May be empty.

PageSize.description: Paper size allowlist. `a4` = ISO A4 (210×297mm), emitted with explicit width/height. Single-variant today; the enum stays extensible.

PageOrientation.description: Which way the paper is turned. `portrait` = upright (the default when absent); `landscape` = turned sideways (Typst `page.flipped`; DOCX swaps the page width/height pair).

FontFamily.description: Curated font-family allowlist matching the bundled font set. `serif` = a serif face, rendered as Times New Roman in both PDF and DOCX with the metric-identical Liberation Serif as fallback (default body text for formal documents; the NĐ30 face); `sans-serif` = a sans face; `monospace` = a fixed-width face. Arbitrary family names are not accepted.

FontSize.description: Curated font-size allowlist (each value is a point size string rendered as Npt). Authors pick from this fixed palette; arbitrary point sizes are intentionally disallowed so previews stay consistent. 8pt/10pt = fine print, 11pt–14pt = body copy, 18pt/24pt = headings/titles.

TextAlign.description: Horizontal alignment for a text/blockquote/rich_text block. `left` = ragged-right (default); `center` = centred; `right` = ragged-left; `justify` = flush both edges.

HeadingAlign.description: Horizontal alignment for a heading or image block. Same meanings as TextAlign but WITHOUT `justify` (justification is meaningless for headings and images). Default is `left` for headings, `center` for images.

ListStyle.description: Flat-list marker turning a block into a list item; consecutive blocks with the same value render as one list. Bulleted: `disc` = filled circle, `circle` = hollow circle, `square` = filled square. Ordered: `decimal` = 1,2,3; `lower-alpha` = a,b,c; `upper-alpha` = A,B,C; `lower-roman` = i,ii,iii; `upper-roman` = I,II,III.

CitationMode.description: How a rich_text block renders inline agent citation markers (`[ID:<uuid>]`) in its bound value. `remove` = strip the markers (default; a finished document never shows raw markers); `link` = resolve each marker to a Markdown link to its cited source document.

SigningFieldType.description: The kind of value a signer fills into an inline signing field. `signature` = a drawn signature (default, historical behaviour); `initials` = drawn initials; `date` = signer-typed date; `text` = signer-typed free text; `number` = signer-typed number; `checkbox` = a tick box. `signature`/`initials` are identity marks (usable as a certificate seal anchor); the rest are typed fills.

InlineMark.description: A composable inline formatting mark; order within a run's `marks` array is irrelevant (the renderer nests them deterministically). `bold`, `italic`, `underline` (touching character underline), `strikethrough`, `code` (monospace inline code), `highlight` (yellow highlight), `underline_rule` (NĐ30 gạch chân — a line a small gap BELOW the text, gap = PageSetup.rule_gap), `subscript` (lowered smaller text), `superscript` (raised smaller text).

Block.description: A typed block in the document flow. Carries a stable `id`, an optional per-block `margins` inset and `condition` gate, plus the kind-specific fields selected by `type` (see BlockKind). On the wire the kind fields are flattened onto this object.

id.description: Stable unique block identifier (UUID v4). Generate a fresh one per block; it anchors editor state and diffing.

margins.description: Optional per-block inset (space between the block box and its surroundings). Absent → the block fills its container. Lengths are absolute (`mm|cm|pt|in`). Unlike page margins a side MAY be negative — it is a signed offset from the page margin, so a negative value bleeds the block toward the page edge — but a negative `top`/`bottom` is floored to "0mm" on save (DOCX cannot express negative vertical spacing); `left`/`right` keep their sign. Not to be confused with a `page_break`'s `page_margins`.

condition.description: Optional "show when" value-producing expression evaluated at render time against the submission payload. Absent → the block always renders. When present, the block renders only if the expression is truthy; an if/else pair is two sibling blocks with complementary conditions. Refused on a section-opening `page_break` and on any block inside a repeating (loop) static-table row (conditions are not evaluated per item).

type.description: Discriminator selecting the block kind (see BlockKind for the allowed values and their payloads): text | heading | blockquote | column_group (legacy alias `row`) | image | table | static_table | page_break | spacer | rich_text.

BlockKind.description: Discriminated union over the block kinds, tagged by `type`. Each branch lists the extra fields valid for that kind (merged onto the Block envelope). New kinds are additive.

oneOf.description: text block — a paragraph of inline `content` nodes. The primary body kind. Becomes a list item when `list_style` is set.

indent.description: First-line/block indent level (unitless step count, 0 = none; the editor emits 0–6). Distinct from an inline `tab`.

list_style.description: When set, makes this paragraph a list item; consecutive same-style blocks form one list.

line_height.description: Line-spacing multiplier as a unitless string. Absent → document default.

content.description: Ordered inline content nodes (runs, links, field-refs, signatures, page-numbers). May be empty for a blank line.

oneOf.description: heading block — a titled paragraph at a given outline `level`.

level.description: Outline depth: 1 = top-level heading, 2 and 3 = deeper/smaller. Drives the level-derived heading size. Any other value is refused at save.

indent.description: Indent level (unitless step count, 0 = none; the editor emits 0–6).

list_style.description: When set, makes this heading a list item.

line_height.description: Line-spacing multiplier as a unitless string. Absent → document default.

content.description: Ordered inline content nodes forming the heading text.

oneOf.description: blockquote block — a quoted passage rendered indented with a left rule.

indent.description: Extra indent level beyond the quote's own indent (0 = none).

content.description: Ordered inline content nodes of the quoted passage.

oneOf.description: column_group block (legacy wire alias `row`) — splits the page width into side-by-side columns, each holding its own block list. Use for multi-column layout; `type` may be either "column_group" (preferred) or "row" (accepted legacy value).

type.description: Selects the column-group kind. Emit "column_group"; "row" is the accepted legacy alias.

gutter.description: Horizontal gap between columns, absolute length. Default "0.5cm".

columns.description: The columns left-to-right (2 to 4 — any other count is refused at save); each carries a `width` and its own nested `blocks`.

oneOf.description: image block — a single image from a template asset or a submission field.

source.description: Where the image bytes come from (tagged by `kind`).

align.description: Horizontal placement of the image (no `justify`). Default `center`.

max_width.description: Maximum rendered width, absolute length; the image scales down to fit. Default "4cm".

oneOf.description: table block — a DATA-BOUND table. Use this when rows come from a runtime array: it loops `array_path` and renders one body row per item, each cell pulling `columns[].item_field_path` (or a per-row `expression`) from the item. Choose this over `static_table` whenever the row count is dynamic.

array_path.description: Dotted path to the array of row objects in the submission payload; one body row is emitted per element.

columns.description: Column definitions left-to-right (header label + which item field / expression fills each body cell). At least one — an empty list is refused at save.

border.description: Uniform border applied to every gridline (rows are runtime-generated, so per-side/per-row control is undefined here). Omitted → renderer default border; `size` 0 → no borders.

header_rows.description: Optional authorable header grid replacing the flat auto header. Cells may span and carry rich content (multi-row merged header). Every header row must tile exactly columns.length columns (a `row_span` reserves its slots on the rows below and may not run past the last header row); a misaligned grid is refused at save (`table_header_grid_shape`). Field-refs in header cells resolve against the top-level payload, not the looped item. Header-cell borders come from the table's uniform `border` (per-cell `borders` are a static-table feature). Omitted/empty → a flat auto header of bold `header_label`s.

oneOf.description: static_table block — an AUTHOR-DRAWN table with an explicit fixed grid of `rows`/`cells`. Cells carry rich block content, support merges (col_span/row_span) and per-cell borders. Use this for hand-laid layouts; a single row may still loop via its `loop_source`. Choose the data-bound `table` instead when every row is generated from one array.

type.description: Selects the author-drawn static table kind.

column_widths.description: Per-column widths in pixels (mirrors the editor's colSizes), rendered as proportional fractions so the table fills the page. Also fixes the grid's column count. Empty/omitted → equal auto-width columns, counted from the first row's column spans.

rows.description: The table rows top-to-bottom. At least one row with at least one column — an empty table is refused at save. At most one row may be a repeating (loop) row.

oneOf.description: page_break block — a hard page break, and, when it carries `orientation` and/or `page_margins`, the start of a new SECTION (a run of pages with its own orientation and page margins). Both fields absent is the plain break, serialised as a bare `{"type": "page_break"}`. Section values are STICKY: they describe the section this break opens and hold until another break changes them; absent means inherit the preceding section, never "reset to the document default". A break that changes nothing stays a plain break; one that does change something is consumed as the section boundary (no extra blank page). A section-opening break must be a top-level body block (refused inside a column or table cell: `section_break_nested`) and may not carry a `condition` (`section_break_condition_unsupported`); a plain break may be conditional. Any page_break is rejected inside header/footer regions.

orientation.description: Orientation of the section this break opens. Absent → inherit the preceding section's orientation (the document's `settings.orientation`, else portrait, for the first break).

page_margins.description: Page margins of the section this break opens, as non-negative absolute lengths. Absent → inherit the preceding section's margins. Named `page_margins` rather than `margins` because the Block envelope already carries `margins` (the per-block inset) and the kind fields are flattened onto the same object.

oneOf.description: spacer block — fixed vertical whitespace.

rich_text block — binds a variable whose value is rendered AS MARKDOWN (headings, lists, blockquotes, bold/italic/code/links parsed from the string), unlike an inline `field_ref` which renders its value as literal plain text. Bind via `path` OR `expression` (expression wins when non-empty). Typical source: an agent's text output.

type.description: Selects the markdown-rendering rich-text block kind.

path.description: Dotted accessor into the submission payload naming the markdown string. Ignored (a hint) when `expression` is present and non-empty.

expression.description: Optional render-time value-producing expression whose result is the markdown source. When non-empty it wins and `path` is ignored.

font_family.description: Base font family the rendered markdown inherits; per-element structure composes on top.

font_size.description: Base body font size; headings still override with their level-derived size.

citation_mode.description: How inline agent citation markers `[ID:<uuid>]` in the bound value render. Default `remove`.

ColumnGroupItem.description: One column inside a column_group: a proportional `width` plus its own nested block list.

width.description: Column width. A fraction (e.g. "1fr", "2fr") shares the row proportionally, or an absolute length for a fixed column.

blocks.description: The blocks stacked inside this column.

ImageSource.description: Where an image block's bytes come from, tagged by `kind`. `template_asset` = a fixed asset uploaded with the template (referenced by `asset_id`); `submission_field` = an image supplied at run time by a form field (referenced by `field_path`) — parseable, but NOT yet renderable, so save refuses it (`feature_not_implemented`); author images as `template_asset`.

oneOf.description: A static image asset stored with the template. Save refuses an `asset_id` that is not attached to the template; import instead DROPS such image blocks (asset bytes do not travel in export files) and reports how many in `dropped_asset_images`, so a cross-installation import loses its logos rather than failing.

asset_id.description: UUID of the uploaded template asset.

oneOf.description: A run-time image pulled from a submission field. Refused at save today (the attachment-resolution path is not implemented, so the image would silently drop from the exported document); do not generate.

field_path.description: Dotted path to the image/file field in the submission payload.

TableColumn.description: One column of a data-bound `table`. Names the item field (or per-row expression) that fills each body cell and the header label, plus optional widths and fills.

item_field_path.description: Field on each row object (relative to the array item) whose value fills the body cell. Ignored when `expression` is present.

header_label.description: Header cell text for this column (used by the flat auto header).

expression.description: Optional per-row expression evaluated against each row object (sibling fields are in scope), rendering a computed column instead of `item_field_path`.

width.description: Optional column width (fraction or absolute length). Absent → auto.

background.description: Fill colour (hex) for this column's body cells. Omitted → no fill.

header_background.description: Fill colour (hex) for this column's header cell. Omitted → no fill.

CellBorder.description: One border spec: thickness, colour and style. `size` is in pixels and `size` 0 removes the border. Absent sub-fields fall back to the renderer default.

size.description: Border thickness in pixels; 0 = no border.

style.description: CSS border-style: `solid` (default look), `dashed`, `dotted`, or `double` (two parallel lines).

CellBorders.description: Per-side cell border overrides (sparse, like the editor's storage): a cell carries only the sides it overrides; every other side inherits the table's default border.

StaticTableRow.description: One row of a static_table (or one header row of a data-bound table). Holds its cells; may optionally repeat as a body template via `loop_source`. A repeating (loop) row is constrained at save (`table_loop_row`): it needs a `loop_as`; its cells may hold only text / heading / blockquote blocks with no inline `signature` and no block `condition`; no cell may carry a `row_span` > 1 and no merged cell from a row above may extend into it; and its cells must tile the table's full column count exactly.

cells.description: The cells of this row left-to-right (accounting for spans of earlier cells).

loop_source.description: When set (non-empty), this row is a body template repeated once per item in the array at this dotted path, which must resolve to an array field of the payload schema (`field_path_not_array` otherwise); its cells resolve plain field-ref paths against each ITEM (e.g. `name`, not `items.name`) and their expressions are evaluated per item. Absent/empty → an ordinary static row. A table holds at most one loop row.

loop_as.description: Name of the per-item scope variable. REQUIRED whenever `loop_source` is set — save refuses a loop row without one (the renderer only falls back to "item" for a stored tree). Must be a plain identifier (a letter or `_`, then letters, digits or `_`) and not the reserved `__i`.

loop_index_as.description: Optional name for the 1-based position of each generated row, so a cell can print it (an "STT"/No. column) via a plain `field_ref` whose `path` is this name, or compute with it in an expression (e.g. `idx * 10`). A `row_index` inline token prints the same counter without naming it. Absent → no named counter (existing templates are unaffected). Only meaningful on a loop row. Must be a plain identifier, not `__i`, not equal to `loop_as`, and not the name of a field the looped item already declares (a collision would make a plain reference and an expression disagree about the same name).

StaticTableCell.description: One cell of a static_table row. Holds rich block content and optional merge spans, fill, and per-side borders.

blocks.description: The cell's content as a nested block list (can hold text, images, even nested tables).

header.description: Header cell (th) — rendered bold. Default false; omit when false.

col_span.description: Horizontal merge span (>= 2). Omit when the cell occupies a single column.

row_span.description: Vertical merge span (>= 2). Omit when the cell occupies a single row.

background.description: Cell fill colour (hex). Omitted → no fill.

borders.description: Per-side border overrides. Omitted → the cell inherits the table's default border on every side.

ContentNode.description: An inline content fragment inside a text/heading/blockquote block, tagged by `type`. `text` is the canonical run (a string with a flat `marks` set); `plain`/`bold`/`italic` are legacy single-mark runs kept parseable; `link` wraps nested inline content; `linebreak`/`tab` are inline whitespace; `signature`/`field_ref`/`page_number`/`row_index` are void inline objects.

oneOf.description: text run — the canonical inline run: a literal string plus a flat set of formatting marks so combined formatting survives round-trips.

marks.description: Formatting marks applied to the whole run; order irrelevant. Absent/empty → plain.

font_family.description: Font family override for this run.

font_size.description: Font size override for this run.

tracking.description: Character spacing (Typst tracking), a length. Negative condenses so a long line fits.

rule_width.description: Authored width for the `underline_rule` line, centred on the marked span. Absent → the rule is as wide as the text it marks, which cannot express a rule matching a phrase on another line. `%` is of the span's own text width. Units pt/mm/cm/in/% — deliberately NOT em, which the DOCX length parser cannot read (an em value would render in PDF and vanish from Word). Non-negative; anything else is refused at save (`invalid_length`).

rule_thickness.description: Per-run `underline_rule` weight. Absent → PageSetup.rule_thickness, then the renderer default. Non-negative absolute length only (`mm|cm|pt|in`) — a weight has no meaningful percentage.

color.description: Text (foreground) colour, hex. Absent → inherited body colour.

background_color.description: Run background colour, hex. An explicit colour takes precedence over the yellow `highlight` mark. Absent → none.

oneOf.description: link run — a hyperlink wrapping nested inline content.

content.description: The inline content rendered as the clickable link text.

oneOf.description: plain run — legacy unformatted text run (kept parseable; new trees emit `text`).
bold run — legacy bold text run (kept parseable; new trees emit `text` with a `bold` mark).
italic run — legacy italic text run (kept parseable; new trees emit `text` with an `italic` mark).
linebreak — a soft line break within the paragraph. Carries no fields.
tab — a fixed horizontal gap at the caret (Word-style mid-line Tab, distinct from block/first-line indent). Carries no fields.

signature — an inline signing field (a markable VOID that reserves space in the flow). `field_type` picks the value the signer fills; when `role` is present+non-empty it becomes an eSign field bound to that role, else a plain reserved area. A selection spanning it carries `marks`/font onto the field so a typed value renders in the surrounding style. Refused inside a header/footer region and inside a repeating (loop) table row.

type.description: Selects an inline signing field. (Wire tag is historically "signature"; `field_type` discriminates the actual kind.)

id.description: Stable eSign field name (unique within the document).

role.description: Signer role this field binds to. Present+non-empty → an eSign-bound field; absent → a plain reserved area.

field_type.description: The value kind the signer fills. Absent → `signature` (drawn), the historical default.

label.description: Caption shown above the field in the editor and passed to eSign as the field label.

required.description: Whether the signer must fill this field. Absent → a per-type default (identity marks required, typed fills optional).

reserved_width.description: Reserved horizontal size: a Typst absolute length OR a space count ("Nsp", measured against the field's font). Absent → default signature width.

reserved_height.description: Reserved vertical size, a Typst absolute length. Absent → a per-type default (marks get drawing room; typed fills sit at ~line height).

marks.description: Inline marks the field renders its filled value in; also the font a space-count width is measured against.

font_family.description: Font family for the filled value.

font_size.description: Font size for the filled value.

oneOf.description: field_ref — an inline VOID that renders a bound value as LITERAL plain text (contrast the rich_text BLOCK, which parses markdown). Bind via a dotted `path` OR an `expression` (expression wins when present). A markable void: a selection spanning it carries `marks`/font onto the chip so a whole line — fixed text plus dynamic fields — formats uniformly.

path.description: Dotted context path resolved type-preserving from the submission payload; a plain path must resolve against the payload schema at save (`field_path_missing`). Inside a repeating table row it resolves against the looped ITEM, and a path equal to the row's `loop_index_as` renders the 1-based row counter. Required on the wire but ignored when `expression` is present (emit "" then).

expression.description: Optional render-time value-producing expression (same engine as computed fields/decision conditions). When present the rendered value is the expression result and `path` is ignored; the `format` mask still applies. Syntax is checked at save. Inside a repeating table row it is evaluated per item, with the row's `loop_index_as` counter in scope.

format.description: Optional display mask for the value: a date mask (e.g. "DD/MM/YYYY") or a number mask (e.g. `#.##0,00 "₫"`). Absent → the raw stored value. An unrecognised mask degrades to the raw value; longer than 64 characters is refused at save (`field_format_too_long`).

marks.description: Inline marks applied to the rendered value (markable void).

font_family.description: Font family for the rendered value.

font_size.description: Font size for the rendered value.

tracking.description: Character spacing; see the text run's `tracking`.

rule_width.description: Authored rule width; see the text run's `rule_width`.

rule_thickness.description: Per-run rule weight; see the text run's `rule_thickness`.

color.description: Text colour (hex); see the text run's `color`.

background_color.description: Background colour (hex); see the text run's `background_color`.

oneOf.description: page_number — an inline render-time counter token (NOT a field-ref path). Compose "Trang X / Y" from literal text plus a current token plus a total token. Meaningful only inside a header/footer region; elsewhere renders as "1".

total.description: false → current page number; true → total page count. Default false; omit when false.

marks.description: Inline marks applied to the rendered counter.

oneOf.description: row_index — an inline render-time counter printing the 1-based position of the generated row (an "STT"/No. column), like `page_number` a token rather than a field-ref path. Valid ONLY inside a cell of a repeating (loop) static-table row; anywhere else it is refused at save (`table_loop_row`) rather than rendering a bare "1". Needs no `loop_index_as` on the row, and carries no start/offset: it always agrees with the row's `loop_index_as` counter and with expressions over it.

marks.description: Inline marks applied to the rendered counter.
